options.title: What is Australia's 5,614 km fence keeping out?
options.first_line: What is Australia's {fact1} kilometre fence keeping out?
options.first_frame: The map of Australia fills the frame and a wire fence draws itself across the south-east, a fence post sign reading the length as it runs.

options.title: Why does one fence cut Australia in two?
options.first_line: Why does one fence cut Australia in two?
options.first_frame: Australia on the map with a single fence line splitting it, the north tinted orange and the south-east green, a dingo on one side and a sheep on the other.

options.title: What is Australia's Dingo Fence keeping out?
options.first_line: Australia built a fence across the whole continent. What is the Dingo Fence keeping out?
options.first_frame: A patrol truck stops at a gate in the fence on the map of Australia, the sign on the gate reading DINGO FENCE, the line running off both edges.

why: A recognisable country, an absurdly long fence you can picture and a real question with the answer held back, while C names the dingo in its title and B shows the dingo and sheep in its first frame, giving the answer away.
